summary: Angeles NF lookout on Mendenhall Peak, built 1936 or 1937; destroyed in the November 1975 Mill/Big Tujunga Fire; foundation, water tank and shack remnants reported on the summit.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin atop a 10-foot open timber tower
facts.status_note: Destroyed in the 1975 fire and not rebuilt; SummitPost describes a concrete foundation, a water tank and the remnants of two small shacks on the summit

access.note: On Angeles National Forest land, reached on foot by forest road and an abandoned road from Dillon Divide; SummitPost describes walking around a gate. No closure is described in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: Drive about 7 miles up Little Tujunga Canyon Road to Dillon Divide and park near the gate; walk the dirt road (3N32) about four miles to Mendenhall Saddle, then the abandoned road about a mile to the summit. The last section, from the gate at Mendenhall Saddle, is overgrown with a couple of washouts (SummitPost).

Brush fire set deliberately in Little Tujunga threatened the lookout; a lookout had to leave her post and was rescued by helicopter

Mill Fire, also called the Big Tujunga Fire, started high in the Angeles Forest on Saturday, November 22, 1975 and burned through Big Tujunga Canyon; razed 43 buildings including the Mendenhall Peak lookout
Lookout destroyed in the Big Tujunga Fire in November 1975; everyone on site evacuated safely; not rebuilt

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS gives 1937 and Angeles Adventures gives 1936. The record keeps FFLOS 1937 as the register date; the story says the sources disagree.
FFLOS calls the 1975 blaze the Big Tujunga Fire; Crescenta Valley Weekly and Angeles Adventures call it the Mill Fire (of Big Tujunga). Dates and place match, so they appear to be the same fire.
FFLOS gives 4,639 ft (1,414 m); Angeles Adventures gives 4,636 ft. The difference is trivial and the record's 1,414 m is kept.

notes_for_editor: Build year is 1937 per FFLOS but 1936 per Angeles Adventures; story says so. Fire name differs (Big Tujunga vs Mill Fire) but both match Nov 1975. The present-day foundation, tank and shack remnants rest on one climbing-site page (SummitPost) with no date visible in the text we read; treat as recent-ish but unverified. Angeles Adventures shows a lookout photo credited to Paul H. Rippens and LA Times photos, but no image URLs or licences were captured, so no photos added. The record's coordinates (34.349622, -118.312309) and Angeles Adventures' (34.348462, -118.313603) differ by about 175 m; not corrected. Access is recorded as public because it is National Forest land reached on foot, not because a source states a public-access rule. Route corrected 2026-10-09: the walk is about four miles of dirt road to Mendenhall Saddle, then about a mile of abandoned road; the first draft left out the dirt-road leg.
